revision_notes: Original 0/Unknown score should be reconsidered: Libya's Law No. 8 of 2014 establishes a 'national database' of all citizens, formed jointly by the Civil Status Authority and the National ID project, containing core identifying data and a unique National ID number, described in law as supplementary to (but distinct from) the Civil Registry. This meets the metadata definition of a population register. However, the database has suffered severe data-quality and governance problems since 2011 (an alleged takeover by armed groups in 2016, allegations of up to a million fraudulent ID numbers, and an ongoing paper-to-electronic reconciliation project, Intilaqa, still incomplete as of September 2024), and Libya's political split affects national consistency. revised_comments: Libya maintains a national identity database, established under Law No. 8 of 2014 and administered jointly by the Civil Status Authority and the National ID project, which assigns a unique National ID Number to every citizen and underpins access to passports, banking, mobile SIM registration and voting. The database has been affected by significant data-integrity and governance challenges since 2011, including an alleged 2016 takeover by armed groups and an ongoing paper-to-electronic reconciliation exercise (Intilaqa) that remained incomplete as of September 2024.
